newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Placer Dome told it is welcome in Philippines.
newsitem.headline: Placer Dome told it is welcome in Philippines.

text.p: President Fidel Ramos has told Canadian mining giant Placer Dome Inc that it is welcome in the Philippines despite a controversy over a waste spill, a presidential spokesman said on Tuesday.

Senior executives from Placer Dome met Ramos on Monday and expressed a desire for the firm to continue doing business in the Philippines, Presidential Press Secretary Hector Villanueva told Reuters by telephone on Tuesday.
"You are welcome to stay," Villanueva quoted Ramos as telling the firm's executives, who were led by Placer president and chief executive officer, John Wilson.

Mine waste from Placer Dome subsidiary Marcopper Mining Corp spilled into a river on the central island of Marinduque in March, causing an outcry among pressure groups worried about the environmental impact.
The company said the spillage was accidental and the waste was not toxic.
But the government has brought criminal charges against three Marcopper executives, including president John Loney, resident manager Steven Reid, both Australians, and senior manager Pedro Hernandez.
Loney and Reid, both nominees of Placer, have since resigned from Marcopper. Placer said they resigned because the company had withdrawn its interest in the mine.
Ramos also suggested that Placer join a business delegation that will accompany Canadian Prime Minister John Cretien when he visits Manila later this year, Villanueva.
Lawyers for Marcopper have asked the court to dismiss the charges against the executives, saying the waste spill was "an act of God" for which no one could be held liable.
They said the spill occurred after an earthquake created fractures in Marcopper's waste reservoir.
The court has yet to rule on the lawyers' motion.
